text:
maya: Quick heads-up — ACME POC kickoff tomorrow. They want ~250 qps steady with spikes to ~400 qps for chat completions. Model they'll test: redwood-3B-q4_0. Avg response ~40 tokens. Need plan for reserved GPUs + autoscale fallback. Also waiting on their security questionnaire (SSO/KMS). Anyone available to size?

noah: I can take throughput sizing. 250 qps * 40 tokens = 10k tokens/s baseline. Confirm latency SLOs and if multi-turn KV caching matters.

maya: P50 <200ms, P95 <500ms. Mostly short turns but there are some multi-turn sessions where KV cache helps. Auth via SAML; they asked about KMS for logs/encryption.

sam: For redwood-3B-q4_0 on A100-40 we typically see ~800-1k tok/s per GPU under latency-optimized config with small batch sizes. For those SLOs I'd push for dedicated reserved GPUs. Quick suggestion: commit to 3 reserved GPUs for baseline (cover 250 qps) and allow autoscale bursts up to 6 GPUs for spikes. Use prewarm slots to avoid cold starts.

eli: Adding the quick math snippet I ran locally: 
```text
peak_qps = 400
avg_tokens = 40
tokens_per_sec = peak_qps * avg_tokens = 16000
gpu_tok_per_sec_est = 4000  # conservative est for latency config
required_gpus = ceil(tokens_per_sec / gpu_tok_per_sec_est) = 4
```
So baseline 3 reserved + burst to 6 covers headroom and node-level variance.

sam: Autoscale knobs I'd propose: min_replicas=3, max_replicas=6, cooldown=60s, target_utilization=0.7. Prewarm 1 slot per AZ. Spot/ephemeral for bursts not ideal given tight P95.

maya: ACME asked about pricing: what's the monthly price delta for committed GPUs vs on-demand? Also asked if we can provide a small POC credit for the 2-week evaluation.

noah: Ballpark: standard commit discount is ~20% on 3+ GPU monthly SKUs. We can usually give a $10k POC credit for strategic proofs. I'll confirm with finance and send a formal quote.

carol: (legal/security) They sent back an SCCQ. Need confirmation on KMS integration, data residency (eu-only?), and audit logs retention. Please attach the SCCQ here and confirm whether Private deploy or Hosted with VPC is planned.

maya: SCCQ link: https://redwood.internal/poc/ACME/sccq — they noted EU data residency and want KMS for key management. They prefer hosted with VPC peering but open to Private if needed.

securitybot: Reminder: Private deployments require SOC2 controls and KMS integration. Please create a ticket in #eng-oncall for provisioning and security review.

eli: A few operational notes:
- AZ preheat: recommend prewarm=1 per AZ for consistent latency.
- Fallback model: provide smaller quantized model (redwood-1.5B-q4) as graceful degradation for extreme overload.
- Cache warmup: enable prefix/KV cache for session continuity.

sam: Example autoscale policy for the runbook: 
```yaml
policy:
  min_replicas: 3
  max_replicas: 6
  scale_metric: tokens/s
  target_utilization: 0.7
  prewarm: 1
  fallback_models: [redwood-1.5B-q4]
```
And add an eval check to failover only if quality drop < threshold.

maya: I'll coordinate schedule with ACME. Next steps: eli to draft capacity plan + cost estimate; noah to confirm discount/credits with finance; carol to review SCCQ and advise on hosted vs private; sam to prepare model fallback config and runbook.

eli: Will do. I'll spin up a proper runbook and post link here when ready. Tentative capacity doc will include per-AZ preheat and warm cache plan.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: preheat job queued for 2026-05-03T10:00Z (job id: pj-99822)

noah: I'll put together a one-pager (traffic assumptions, recommended commit, price ballpark, POC credit) and ping finance/legal.

maya: Thanks all. One small follow-up from ACME — they want preheat across 3 AZs with AZ-affinity and cross-AZ fallback. Add that to runbook. :thumbsup:

sam: Noted. We'll set prewarm=1 per AZ and implement a cross-AZ failover window of 30s for traffic redistribution.

eli: Also, avoid spot for latency-critical pools — use reserved for baseline and on-demand reserved pool for burst.

maya: Perfect. Put any blockers here and I'll escalate to AM if needed.

noah: I'll confirm finance by EOD.

maya: Great — thanks everyone.
